articleTitle: Overview of the Mars laser communications demonstration project
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present an overview of the Mars laser communications demonstration (MLCD.) a joint project between NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology (JPL), and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Lincoln Laboratory (MIT/LL). MLCD's goal is to demonstrate the first high-rate, free-space laser communications link from deep space back to Earth. The lasercom flight terminal will be flown on the Mars telecommunications orbiter, to be launched by NASA in 2009, and will demonstrate a technology which has the potential of vastly improving NASA's ability to communicate throughout the solar system.

articleTitle: Free-space laser propagation: atmospheric effects
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Interest in high-data-rate free-space optical (FSO) laser communication systems has grown significantly in recent years because of the advantages offered by FSO systems over radio frequency (RF) systems. Most advantages are simple consequences of the short wavelengths associated with optical waves. However, there are some drawbacks that arise from the shorter wavelengths used in FSO systems. This article presents advantages and disadvantages and its effect.

articleTitle: Practical considerations of retroreflector choice in modulating retroreflector systems
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Optical modulating retroreflectors (MRRs) were demonstrated before the invention of the laser, but were restricted to short distances and low data rates. Recent advances in optoelectronic devices and free space optics have greatly increased the capabilities of MRR systems. Several modulator technologies have been used in MRR systems and compared elsewhere. In this discussion, practical considerations of the two types of bulk optic retroreflectors used in km-range MRRs were compared: corner cube retroreflectors and cat's eye retroreflectors. Examples of MRR systems using each type are given.

articleTitle: 1.5-photons/bit photon-counting optical communications using Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a photon-counting communications link using Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes. High-efficiency pulse-position modulation and forward error correcting codes are used to demonstrate a receiver sensitivity of 1.5 incident photons/bit.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet comm links for distributed sensor networks
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Free-space ultraviolet communication exploits atmospheric scattering and absorption to achieve modest data rates with non-line-of-sight transmit-receive geometries. We introduce the ultraviolet communication concept and report on test bed measurements made outdoors in full daylight.

articleTitle: Design for a 5-Watt PPM transmitter for the Mars laser communications demonstration
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The Mars laser communication demonstration uses a PPM communication system operating from 25-kbps to greater than 30-Mbps at 1064-nm with a 5-W transmitter. Design, performance, and qualification of the transmitter subsystems are described.

articleTitle: Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes for photon-counting communications
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Arrays of photon-counting avalanche photodiodes enable laser-communications receivers with unprecedented sensitivity at 1.06-/spl mu/m wavelength. Arrays with 64 elements were fabricated in the InGaAsP/InP materials system and were bump-bonded to a custom CMOS integrated circuit. The integrated circuit uses a novel nonblocking architecture to continuously report both time-of-arrival for incoming photons as well as their spatial location on the array. Near room temperature, the best detectors have: 45% photon detection efficiency, 65-kHz dark count rate, and a 1.6-/spl mu/s reset time to avoid after-pulsing.

articleTitle: Simple, small size, low cost and low time jitter optical pulse generator with wide range tunable repetition rate
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We have developed an compact ultra-low time-jitter pulse generator using LD and self-pulse feedback mechanism. Sub-picosecond low time jitters are successfully observed at any modulation range of between 0.5- and 3-GHz. The pulse generator's size and cost are similar to conventional LD module.

articleTitle: All-optical digital 3-input AND gate using sum- and difference-frequency generation in a PPLN waveguide
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an all-optical bit-wise 3-input AND gate using a single periodically-poled-lithium-niobate (PPLN) waveguide as a nonlinear optical element. Our module generates output '1' bits only when all inputs are '1', with negligible power penalty.

articleTitle: Signal statistics and sequence estimation in intensity modulated fiber optic links containing a single optical pre-amplifier
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A natural criterion of performance optimization in a communication system is that of minimizing the probability of error. In this paper, the authors derive the signal statistics by means of Karhunen-Loeve expansions such that the signal waveforms and the noise before the square-law detector are projected onto a set of orthonormal basis.

articleTitle: LDES: a prototype array optical receiver for the Mars laser communications demonstration program
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In 2009, NASA will launch an optical communications payload to Mars capable of supporting data rates of 1 to 30 Megabits per second. A key element of the Mars laser communications demonstration (MLCD) project is the development of a distributed optical receiver array known as LDES: link development and evaluation system. This paper describes the LDES system, discusses the key technical challenges in its implementation, and shows the performance of hardware developed for the receiver system.

articleTitle: Adaptive optics for daytime deep space laser communications from Mars
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The application of adaptive optics to the daytime deep space link is analyzed. Theoretical results show up to 8.4 dB gains for 64 PPM formats under daytime sky background conditions at 3 degrees sun angle.

articleTitle: The Mars lasercom terminal
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present the Mars lasercom terminal preliminary design that demonstrates high-rate optical communications from Mars and provide NASA with the experience necessary to develop future operational deep-space optical communication systems.

articleTitle: Turning Palomar into a deep-space optical receiver
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The approach for adapting the 200-inch Hale telescope, located at Mt. Palomar, CA to support a deep space optical communications project is outlined. Considerations include protecting the telescope for daytime operations and limiting the amount of background detected by the receiver.

articleTitle: Rate adjustable NRZ-DPSK modulation scheme with fixed interferometer
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A novel rate adjustable NRZ-DPSK modulation scheme using a single fixed delay interferometer is presented. This approach realizes a higher sensitivity than other rate agile non-coherent modulation formats. Initial proof-of-concept results are provided.

articleTitle: Optical isolator independent of input polarization direction utilizing a quarter-wave plate
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A conventional optical isolator is composed of a pair of polarizers whose transmission axes make an angle of 45/spl deg/ with each other and a Faraday 45/spl deg/ rotator sandwiched by the polarizers. Hence, the insertion loss of an optical isolator significantly varies depending on the polarization angle of the input light. On the other hand, the authors have found an interesting phenomenon that when an elliptically polarized light is launched into a quarter-wave plate followed by a polarizer, the output light power is kept constant regardless of the principal axis direction of the input light when the birefringence axis of the quarter-wave plate and the transmission axis of the polarizer make an angle of 45/spl deg/. Utilizing this unique phenomenon, input polarization direction dependence of the insertion loss of an optical isolator is reduced from 17 dB to 0.4 dB by attaching a quarter-wave plate in front of a conventional optical isolator.

articleTitle: Highly-coherent optical terminal design status and outlook
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: After 30 years of development coherent satellite laser terminals will verified in orbit in 2006. General design constraints for space communication optical terminals are reviewed and the design and programmatics of the beacon-less coherent laser crosslink terminals are detailed.

articleTitle: Fiber ring based optical frequency comb generator with comb line spacing tunability
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A fiber ring based optical frequency comb generator with tunability in comb line spacing, fast tuning of 10 MHz per step with speed much better than 0.1 s, and a high coherence is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Compact laser transceiver for mobile terminals
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The possibility to provide a high-speed laser communication to the mobile terminals on aircrafts, ships, trains and cars is studied and small and light-weight laser terminal is developed for a high-altitude stratospheric platform test flight. The laser terminal onboard is consist of an optical antenna, two-axes gimbals and optical receiver and is capable of analogue signal transmission compatible to digital TV signal at UHF band. A preliminary result of the test flight up to a 4-km altitude is also reported.

articleTitle: Timing distribution and RF-synchronization with mode-locked lasers
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Large-scale timing distribution and synchronization based on mode-locked lasers is discussed. The noise of low-jitter mode-locked lasers is characterized. Amplitude-to-phase conversion in photodetection is measured and a scheme avoiding this conversion is proposed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb generation from modelocked diode lasers - techniques applications
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This paper discusses the development of modelocked semiconductor lasers to generate optical frequency combs for applications in photonic signal processing. Key in our approach is a high Q cavity, supermode suppression and low spontaneous emission.

articleTitle: Terahertz repetition rate optical pulse train generation based on comb-like profiled fiber
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally generate a 1-THz, 9/spl square/fs pulse train based on the CPF. To the authors' knowledge, this is the smallest duration amongst the continuously operated optical pulse sources at a terahertz repetition rate ever reported.

articleTitle: Photon-counting detectors for optical communications
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Photon counting direct detection allows communications past the classical limit of 2.88 bits/photon, and is an attractive solution for photon starved optical communications links, as in deep space scenarios. High bandwidth communications requires a corresponding high bandwidth detector with a high saturation fluence, especially in the presence of a large background noise flux, as is encountered during daytime optical link operations. Traditional photon counting optical detectors, such as Geiger mode avalanche photodiodes and photomultiplier tubes, have been developed primarily for low rate / low flux applications such as fluorescence spectroscopy. Ground based detectors have an additional requirement of large area since a single spatial mode transmit signal is scattered into many spatial modes by atmospheric turbulence, resulting in a solid angle times area (Lagrange) invariant that must be processed by the optical receiver train. As there is a physical limit to the solid area (2/spl pi/ steradians for single side illumination), there is thereby a corresponding minimum detector area that is proportional to the number of spatial modes.

articleTitle: Signal and background levels for the Mars laser communications demonstration (MLCD)
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We examine signal, /spl lambda//sub s/, and background, /spl lambda//sub b/ photon flux rates incident upon the Palomar receive terminal over different phases and operating conditions of the planned demonstration. The variation of [/spl lambda//sub s/,/spl lambda//sub b/] is translated into link performance.

articleTitle: Coherent optical communications & signal processing using optical frequency combs
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This paper discusses use of optical frequency combs generated by modelocked semiconductor lasers for coherent photonic signal processing applications. Targeted applications lie in areas of metrology, optical sampling, arbitrary waveform generation and communications using coherent detection.

articleTitle: 1.55 /spl mu/m photomixer sources for mm-wave heterodyne detection and frequency conversion with Schottky diodes
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Millimetre-wave signals from high speed InP/InGaAs uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes (UTC-PD) have been used to drive Schottky diodes for harmonic generation, the down conversion of an 80 GHz tone and the heterodyne detection of 183 GHz radiation.

articleTitle: SIMBA: A new technique for ultrashort pulse characterization
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A novel technique (spectral interferometry using minimum-phase based algorithm, or SIMBA) to recover the phase and magnitude of the electric-field profile of weak ultra-short laser pulses is presented. SIMBA involves measuring with an optical spectrum analyzer (OSA) the power spectrum of a sequence consisting of a dummy pulse followed by the sample pulse to be characterized. The sample pulse profile is then uniquely retrieved either with the analytical Hubert transformation or with a simple iterative error-reduction algorithm applied to this spectrum. SIMBA presents several significant advantages over existing techniques: it does not require a reference pulse with a known profile, which reduces measurement time and complexity significantly; the experimental set-up is simple and has no moving parts; data processing is fast, allows real-time characterization, and exhibits a lower sensitivity to measurement noise; it can be used to characterize ultraweak pulses; it discriminates between a pulse and its time reversal; and it can characterize a series of multiple pulses with a single OSA measurement.

articleTitle: A frequency comb in the extreme ultraviolet
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate higher order harmonic generation directly from a 110 MHz femtosecond oscillator using a buildup cavity. This is an important step towards high precision spectroscopy and high power coherent sources in the extreme ultraviolet.

articleTitle: Photonic multiple beam forming systems for broadband RF antenna arrays
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Two broadband, sparse array, multiple-beamforming, optical processors are presented. They enable squint-free, true-time delay beamforming of large, randomly-spaced antenna arrays by compensating the frequency-dependent scale factor of the RF images produced by a Fourier optical imager.

articleTitle: Optical signal processing based on temporal and spectral Talbot phenomena in fibers
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Time-domain and frequency-domain Talbot phenomena in optical fibers can be exploited for several signal processing applications, including pulse repetition-rate multiplication, microwave frequency upshifting and free-spectral-range tuning of frequency combs. The fundaments and applications of these phenomena are reviewed.

articleTitle: Progress on indium and barium single ion optical frequency standards
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report progress on /sup 115/In/sup +/ and /sup 137/Ba/sup +/ single ion optical frequency standards using all solid-state sources. Both are free from quadrupole field shifts and together enable a search for drift in fundamental constants.

articleTitle: ps/nm tunable dispersion compensator using cascaded Gires-Tournois etalons
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We proposed a novel tunable dispersion compensator using cascaded, thermally tunable Gires-Tournois etalons. We present results demonstrating tunability over the range +2000 ps/nm to -2000 ps/nm with a usable window of 0.2 nm at 50 GHz channel spacing.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of a single Al/sup +/ ion via coupling to Be/sup +/
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We perform precision spectroscopy on /sup 27/Al/sup +/ with the aid of a /sup 9/Be/sup +/ ion. Using sympathetic cooling and quantum state transfer, we efficiently interrogate the /sup 1/So /spl rarr/ /sup 3/Pi and /sup 1/So /spl rarr/ /sup 3/Po transitions.

articleTitle: Analysis and synthesis of optical lattice filters with adjustable gains
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Propagation of light in optical waveguides and scattering of light at interfaces have been modeled by a class of lattice filter structures. In this paper, the authors propose a recursive algorithm retrieving parameters of each 2-input, 2-output stage of the structure from the coefficients of the given transfer function. A generalized form of the single-input, single-output lattice filter is shown in this paper. The input-output transfer function is defined as the reflection transfer function.

articleTitle: Simulaltaneous generation of ultra-low noise optical pulse and microwave signal
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we describe the coupled opto-electronic oscillator (COEO) that simultaneous generates both low-jitter optical pulses and low phase noise microwave signal. It has been shown that the mode-locked laser has a microwave transfer property similar to that of a high-Q microwave resonator, which is responsible for the ultra-low noise achieved in the COEO system.

articleTitle: High-frequency local oscillator transmission for the Atacama large millimeter array (ALMA)
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The Atacama large millimeter array (ALMA) is an international radio astronomical facility currently under construction in Chile [Wooten, A et al., 2005]. Due to the unprecedented combination of high frequency and long baselines, and the requirement that it operate as an interferometer, the array requires Local Oscillators (LO) and LO references with extremely low phase-noise and phase drift. The LO requirements, design implementation, and preliminary results are presented.

articleTitle: Robust and precise length correction of 25-km fiber for distribution of local oscillator
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In order to distribute local oscillators for the phased-array radio telescopes, the cycle-slip free fiber length stabilization system has been developed. The length of the 25-km fiber was precisely measured by the Michelson interferometer with a digital phase frequency discriminator, and the length fluctuation of which was suppressed down to 2.5 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Demonstration of an all-optical interface between wavelength-hopping time-spreading optical CDMA and WDM networks
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate efficient, high-performance format conversion from wavelength-hopping time-spreading (WHTS) optical CDMA to NRZ using a terahertz optical asymmetric demultiplexer (TOAD), with 1 dB power penalty. Schemes for interfacing WHTS and WDM networks are presented.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a 2D incoherent transparent OCDMA path router
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: With the increasing demand in services and the growth of traffic flows in telecommunication networks, optical code division multiple access (OCDMA) has become a widely studied multiplexing technique. Developing the technology to make OCDMA a viable multiplexing scheme for mesh networks could provide the increased flexibility and scalability needed for MANs and LANs. In this paper, the authors proposed a router architecture that provides a flexible all-optical method in creating reconfigurable paths, reducing switching delays and node complexity.

articleTitle: The effect of uplink fading on the pointing and tracking system of the Mars lasercom terminal
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We study the effect of atmospheric fading on the pointing and tracking system of the Mars lasercom terminal. We show system performance with varying atmospheric turbulence. Algorithms to mitigate errors caused by fading are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Photonic analog-to-digital conversion
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Potentially THz-regime optical quantizing and coding for ultrafast analog-to-digital conversion using fiber-optic nonlinear loop mirror is presented. Emerging applications would be in high bit rate (<40 Gb/s) optical communications. 3-bit AD conversion at 10-Giga-sample-per-second is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Free-space-optical networks: some capacity considerations
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Free space-optical networks deployed as a mesh topology are well suited for ultra broadband last mile business and residential services. Considered are several capacity and mobility management aspects of such networks.

articleTitle: Dual-DPSK-OOK transceiver for free-space optical networks
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We propose a reconfigurable dual-DPSK-OOK transceiver sub-system. The concept is demonstrated at 10 Gb/s, and offers a simple and cost effective approach for building a flexible satellite-terrestrial optical network.

articleTitle: Tailoring of the power spectral density of ultrawideband RF and microwave signals
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate that chirped RF waveforms, synthesized via optical frequency-to-time and optical-to-electrical conversion, lead to increases in RF energy of up to 10/spl times/ and RF power spectral density up to 10 dB as compared to ultrawideband impulses.

articleTitle: Achieving comparable global accuracy in the split-step Fourier simulation of optical fiber communication channel
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Optical communication system design is a challenging task because there is no general analytical solution for the nonlinear and dispersive fiber channel. Although there has been progress in analytical channel models such as Volterra series model and other variants of the perturbation model, numerical simulations are still extensively used in channel characterization, equalization and system design. In this paper, the authors are interested in finding ways to control local and global errors when the same simulation is repeated for a range of different system parameter values.

articleTitle: Application of erasure decoding in fiber optical systems with FEC
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Error-and-erasure decoding scheme is first proposed in optical receivers using FEC. Almost 1.3 dB of additional coding gain at output BER of 10/sup -12/ can be estimated for the intact RS (255,239) coding scheme.

articleTitle: Optical frequency control by using optical single-sideband modulation technique
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We propose an optical frequency sweeper with an optical single-sideband modulator, by sweeping electric signal frequency in the driving circuit. Undesired sidebands due to electric phase errors can be compensated by optical bias control.

articleTitle: Laser systems for gravitational wave detection
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This paper reports on the status of the Virgo detector, now on its commissioning phase: we describe the setup, the implemented functions, we discuss the spectral resolution measured during the last commissioning data taking, we present some of the practical issues. We show the role of the optical metrology in the instrument. Its first role is on the apparatus design: we show how the optical design of Virgo improves the sensitivity compared to a simple Michelson interferometer. The laser beam needs to be very stable, in the detection band 10 Hz-10 kHz: beam pointing, power stability and frequency stability. We show that this can be achieved using very stable references and enhanced feedback loops. Optical metrology is also necessary to measure the mirror substrates and surfaces and ensure that they have the required properties: roughness, absorption, and local defects, transmission maps. The output of optical simulations using these maps can be compared with in-situ measurement of some global parameters: cavity finesses, mirror curvatures, contrast defect.

articleTitle: Optical carrier suppressed single sideband (O-CS-SSB) modulation using a hyperfine blocking filter based on a virtually-imaged phased-array (VIPA)
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a novel O-CS-SSB modulation with sideband suppression of /spl sim/28 dB at only a 2.9 GHz frequency offset and strong carrier suppression of /spl sim/30 dB lower in power than the unsuppressed sideband.

articleTitle: Active optical lattice filters
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Highly integrated, novel architectures for optical filtering can leverage structure, gain and variable delays to provide a multi-use photonic platform. Hardware and software results are presented.

articleTitle: High frequency photonic microwave oscillators based on WGM resonators
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This paper studies the applications of novel photonic microwave oscillators containing high-Q whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonators intended to produce low noise high frequency MW signals ranging from X-band to W-band. We theoretically compare the fundamental as well as practical restrictions on the performance of both an optical hyper-parametric oscillator based on a nonlinear high-Q WGM resonator and an "oscillator" based on two lasers locked to the same linear WGM resonator to produce stable MW beat signals. Finally, we report on a proof of the principle experiment where we realized the hyper-parametric oscillator generating /spl sim/ 10 GHz signals with 200 Hz linewidth and -110 dBc/Hz noise floor at 1 MHz from /spl sim/ 10 GHz carrier.

articleTitle: Effect of laser linewidth reduction systems on coherence length and interferometer noise
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We analyze the effect of linewidth reduction systems on the degree of coherence of a laser and the noise levels measured at the output of an interferometer. We show results computed from the power spectral density of frequency noise measured on a DFB fiber laser and a DFB semiconductor laser narrowed with electrical feedback. Results show that the increase of coherence and interferometer noise is significant only over specific range of interferometer length, and that the improvement of interferometer noise might be proportionally much less important than the improvement in linewidth and coherence length.

articleTitle: Spectral equalization for all order PMD compensation
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Spectral polarization and phase equalization using pulse shaping techniques are applied to all order PMD compensation. Two programmable double-pass pulse shapers are used in series to correct a PMD distorted sub-picosecond pulse.

articleTitle: Linear and low-power nonlinear processing for optical code division multiplexing (O-CDMA), short pulse transmission, and measurement
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This talk discusses the examples of our work on linear optical signal processing using pulse shapers (O-CDMA encoding and dispersion compensation) and low power nonlinear processing using PPLN waveguides (O-CDMA waveform discrimination and ultrashort pulse measurement).

articleTitle: Physical-layer routing issues in free-space optical communication networks
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The application of free-space optical communications to interconnect applications may be essential regardless of system scale. For different length scales, we explore the optimal use of channel resources, various physical impairments, and potential reconfigurable routing challenges.

articleTitle: Optical and microwave frequency stability: some constraints
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Optical frequency references achieve the best frequency stability of any oscillators by taking advantage of high Q = v/sub 0///spl Delta/v optical resonances. These systems are beginning to run into fundamental and technical limitations which are discussed.

articleTitle: A rapidly reconfigurable multicast capable photonic switched interconnect design and operating principles
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present design criteria for a rapidly reconfigurable, serial gated timeslot tuner useful for various applications such as reconfigurable OTDM, OCDMA networks and photonic switched interconnects. Feasible multicast combinations and valid control signals are derived.

articleTitle: Earth-image tracking in the IR for deep space optical communications
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Sub-microradian level laser beam pointing to an Earth-based receiver is required for deep space optical communications. This requires a beacon emanated from Earth towards the spacecraft. The beacon could be a laser or reflected sunlight from Earth. Earth image tracking in the visible is hampered by significant albedo variations and/or crescent Earth image yielding large central errors. Here, we report results of Earth-image tracking in the infrared (8 to 13 micron) region of the spectrum with the aim of substantially alleviating the two challenges mentioned earlier.

articleTitle: Low cost transmitter and receiver for a short-range optical wireless communications and their year evaluation results
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: There have been continuing efforts for using the optical wireless (OWL) or free-space communication as an effective way of connecting subscribers to a fiber backbone. Poor link availability in a hostile weather environment is still an issue for OWL link. Various schemes including the use of RF backup link to improve the availability have been proposed. This paper presents a designed low cost, short-range OWL transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx). Standard packaging techniques were used for mounting optical components and communication devices to cut down the manufacturing cost. The aperture size of the Tx and Rx was /spl sim/5 cm. The beam divergence, wavelength, and calculated link margin for 120 m are 2 mrad, 3 dB and 1310 nm, respectively. Details of evaluation results in bad weather conditions including a record snow fall, record fog, and cloud burst rains are presented.

articleTitle: Amplitude and phase noise of RF photodiodes operated in compression
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present a study of amplitude and residual phase noise in RF photodetectors. At 1 GHz, the noise spectra of p-i-n photodiodes were measured and found to vary with the level of space charge induced RF compression.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurements of 1.55 /spl mu/m diode laser acetylene standards
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Absolute frequency measurements have been made on a pair of acetylene-stabilized diode lasers, using a combination of a frequency chain and femtosecond comb system, together with a passive optical frequency comb generator.

articleTitle: Null coupler devices with anti-symmetric Bragg gratings for optical filtering and encoding systems
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Optical devices integrating multiple signal processing functions onto one chip are desirable. We present a novel integrated optic device to filter and encode signals optically with performance competitive with previous demonstrations.

articleTitle: Advances in electro-optic modulator based frequency combs
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the author introduces the improved optical frequency comb generator (OFCG). The OFCG is based on a Ti diffused LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide electro-optic phase modulator in which coated mirrors on both end facets of the modulator form a Fabry-Perot cavity. It offers significant advantages in terms of lowered drive voltages and higher mechanical stability as compared with bulk-type OFCG.

articleTitle: Frequency-stabilized, erbium-doped fiber laser comb for optical frequency metrology
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A passively mode-locked Er:fiber laser is frequency-stabilized to a stability of 3/spl times/10/sup -13/ at 1 s. Application to the frequency measurement of an I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser is described.

articleTitle: Applications of temporal imaging in optical signal processing
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the authors use temporal imaging concepts in building the novel instrumentation for optical signal processing. Two temporal imaging devices are used, time-lenses and time-prisms. For one instrument, the authors use a time-lens to build a multiwavelength pulse generator ideal for WDM parallel processing that eliminates the need for mode-locking or nonlinear spectrum generation used in current similar sampling instruments. In another device, the authors use a time-prism pair to achieve a programmable ultrafast optical delay line.

articleTitle: High-speed, electronic arbitrary waveform generation using time-domain processing of ultrashort optical pulses
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Ultra wideband (UWB) microwave signals are receiving much attention for their potential use in both radar systems and high-speed data links. The currently available arbitrary waveform generation (AWG) devices operates up to only a few gigahertz. The desire to create UWB signals with carrier frequencies in the 10s of GHz and fractional bandwidths approaching 100% suggests investigating microwave-photonic approaches. In this paper, the authors demonstrate a method for electrical AWG with independent envelope and carrier control though the manipulation of wide bandwidth optical pulses in a time-domain processor.

articleTitle: Optical lattice clock
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report on the precision spectroscopy of the 5s/sup 2/ /sup 1/S/sub o/(F=9/2)-5s5p /sup 3/P/sub o/(F=9/2) clock transition of /sup 87/Sr atoms trapped in a one-dimensional optical lattice and discuss its prospects as a future optical clock.

articleTitle: Stabilization of carrier-envelope phase by locking the differenced frequency femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser with TV-Rb clock
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The carrier-envelope phase and repetition rate of Ti:sapphire laser were locked with a TV-Rb clock. By differenced frequency a home-made ultrabroadband femtosecond laser, we enable to develop a compact frequency comb combined the clock.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurements of the /sup 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 0/ optical clock transition at 578 nm in neutral Yb
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This work has focused on two atoms, Sr and Yb, due in part to the relatively high abundance of their odd isotopes, the use of which is necessary for appreciable direct excitation probability. The Sr clock transition has been measured (with an uncertainty of 20 kHz) using atoms in a magneto-optic trap (MOT), and has been excited with atoms confined in a one dimensional lattice. Here we report direct excitation of the Yb clock transition (at 578 nm) with atoms in a second-stage MOT, and the first fs-laser comb-based absolute measurements of the clock frequency for two different isotopes. These measurements lead to a nearly millionfold improvement in our knowledge of the transition frequencies, an important step toward Doppler-free spectroscopy of Yb atoms in a lattice.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband signal detection using photonic signal preprocessing
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Photonic time-stretch processor can be used to slow down electrical ultra-wideband waveform before it is captured by an electronic digitizer. Using this technique, a real-time transient digitizer with a record one-tera-sample/sec sampling rate is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Sub-hertz optical frequency comparisons between two trapped /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ ions
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Two single-ion optical frequency standards are compared in order to investigate systematic frequency shift effects. Without externally applied perturbations, a mean frequency difference of 0.26(42) Hz is observed, corresponding to a relative agreement of 3.8(6.1) /spl middot/10/sup -16/.

articleTitle: Laser stabilization of the local oscillator for an optical atomic clock
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: This paper demonstrates an ultrastable diode laser system for an optical atomic clock. This laser exploits a novel mounting configuration and is limited by the thermal noise of the cavity to which it is locked. Our measurements show the reality of Hz-level linewidth measurements between lasers of different colors located in different rooms.

articleTitle: Strontium ion optical frequency standard with Hz-level uncertainty
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The frequency of the 674 nm 5s/sup 2/S1/2-4d/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ electric quadrupole clock transition in a single cold /sup 88/Sr/sup +/ ion, with the quadrupole frequency shift nulled, has been measured with a fractional uncertainty of 3.4/spl times/10/sup -15/.

articleTitle: Spectral line-by-line pulse shaping
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate spectral line-by-line pulse shaping. The shaped pulses overlap in time, which leads to observable fluctuations due to comb-offset frequency variations. Preliminary results of arbitrary waveform generation based on this technique are also presented.

articleTitle: Spacing-adjustable birefringence comb filters using a bidirectional dual-pass fiber configuration
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present experimental and simulation results on a cascadable approach to generate birefringence comb filters with widely adjustable wavelength spacing. Up to 12 different spacings have been achieved using 2 segments of polarization-maintaining fibers.

articleTitle: Frequency comb generator for calibration of laser frequency standards
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We describe the frequency comb generator at MIKES, with which laser frequency standards at 633 nm and 532 nm were measured. Frequencies were found to be within 0.2 kHz from the CIPM values for R(56)32-0 a/sub 10/ and R(127)11-5 a/sub 16/. An optical amplifier was developed for measurement of 633 nm standards.

articleTitle: Fiber laser frequency combs and their control
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Fiber laser-based frequency combs can provide a comb of well defined spectral lines across the near-infrared, including the telecommunication band. We discuss these frequency combs with an emphasis on the mechanisms used to phase-lock the combs.

articleTitle: Digital signal processing using periodically-poled lithium-niobate waveguides
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Periodically-poled lithium-niobate waveguides can be used as a high-speed, low-noise optical mixer. We discuss the recent advances in device characteristics as well as a several optical-signal-processing applications, including: wavelength conversion, time (de)multiplexing, data header recognition and writing, addition, subtraction, and code conversion.

articleTitle: Active optical lattice filters as programmable ODE solvers
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Take a two stage active Dowling-MacFarlane optical lattice filter with fixed transmission and reflection coefficients and with a stable all pole (in the open left half plane) transfer function in transmission. Consider a second order ordinary differential equation with a stable all pole transfer function and consider a bounded bandlimited input signal. To find an approximate solution to the ODE with zero initial conditions optically, we introduce the following procedure in solving the higher order differential equations using filters with more stages.

articleTitle: Multi-mode multi-channel fiber dispersion compensation using spatial-spectral holography
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A spatial spectral holographic approach to modal multiplexing and dispersion compensation of multiple signals launched into multi-mode fiber is presented.

articleTitle: IIR filter model for the generalized Michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Michelson interferometer is widely used to implement wavelength interleaver, and its different variants have been investigated from physicist's point of view. From signal processing prospect, the Michelson interferometer can be viewed as a special kind of infinite impulse response (IIR) filter. In this article, the IIR filter model of the generalized Michelson interferometer is developed. With this model, researchers would gain more insights regarding Michelson interferometer performance evaluation and increase their degree of freedom in Michelson interferometer design.

articleTitle: Scintillation suppression in a free-space optical link with a saturated SOA
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Based on a gain saturated semiconductor optical amplifier, we propose a simple approach for scintillation suppression of atmospheric turbulence channels. System performance improvement up to 2.5 Gb/s has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Prospects of quantum computing using planar devices
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: A novel description of quantum computing based on PLC technology is presented, demonstrating the correspondence between quantum mechanics and the coupled wave theory. Applications such as quantum Fourier transform and quantum key distribution are given.

articleTitle: Coherence properties of white light continuum generation in tapered fibers in the fs and ps regime
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We present an experimental study of the pulse-to-pulse phase and the amplitude noise of supercontinua generated in tapered fibers. We put our emphasis on the comparison of pumping with fs and ps pulses, respectively.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of an acetylene-stabilized laser at 1542 nm
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The absolute frequency of an acetylene-stabilized laser is measured using femtosecond combs based on mode-locked Ti:sapphire and fiber lasers. The acetylene-stabilized laser serves as an important optical frequency standard for telecommunication applications.

articleTitle: Highspeed optical micro-cell wireless system for moving user access terminal with VCSELs and receivers array
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Multiple highspeed optical wireless access terminals by using VCSELs- and receivers- array are proposed by using optical micro-cell systems. Controland data-multi-beams directions are quickly controlled by electronic matrix switches of HUB-node and LD/PD/lens array of end-node.

articleTitle: Optical frequency metrology using spectrally tailored continuum from a nonlinear fiber grating
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report the significant enhancement (-24 dB) of the optical beat note between a 657-nm CW laser and the tailored continuum generated with a nonlinear fiber Bragg grating. The same continuum is used to stabilize the offset frequency of a Cr:forsterite femtosecond laser.

articleTitle: Measurement of the frequency of acetylene transitions at 1540 nm with a mode-locked Cr:YAG laser
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: An optical frequency comb from a mode-locked Cr:YAG laser is used to produce a frequency atlas for the region of 1520-1550 nm through measurements of frequency differences for transitions in /sup 12/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ and /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/.

articleTitle: Programmable generation of (ultra-)fast optical pulse bursts by time-domain phase-only filtering
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a fiber-based phase-only filtering technique for generating customized (ultra)fast optical pulse bursts, where the repetition rate and temporal envelope of the generated sequences can be controlled and tuned electronically via EO phase modulation.

articleTitle: Stable distribution of low jitter frequency standards over optical fiber networks
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the authors used the optical fiber as the transfer medium. In the first set of experiments, a microwave frequency standard was placed on the pulse repetition rate (comb spacing) of a mode-locked fiber laser. The authors then compared this method of encoding with simple modulation of a continuous wave laser and have found a marked improvement with the pulsed case. This improvement is due to reduction in the average power on the photodetectors necessary for a given SNR of the detected RF harmonic. By proper dispersion control, the shortest pulse can be delivered to the photodetector which in turn produces the highest SNR with the lowest average power. This result is now limited by the noise floor of the microwave measurement system.

articleTitle: 80 Gb/s optical clock recovery in the presence of polarization fluctuations
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report an 80 Gb/s optical clock recovery system using two-photon absorption in a silicon photodiode, and we theoretically and experimentally quantify the system performance in the presence of polarization fluctuations.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standards based on ultra-cold strontium atoms
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: As a key component of a strontium based optical clock, we have developed an apparatus which allows laser cooling and trapping of more than 10/sup 7/ /sup 88/Sr atoms to temperatures below 1 /spl mu/K. Using this system, we have performed the first high accuracy measurement of the /sup 88/Sr /sup 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 1/ clock transition using an ultra-cold sample. Detailed descriptions of both the measurement technique and corresponding systematic uncertainties is provided. In addition, by varying the density of the ultra-cold /sup 88/Sr sample over a range of three orders of magnitude we obtain the first definitive measurement of a density-related frequency shift and linewidth broadening of an optical clock transition in an ultra-cold alkaline earth system. Spectroscopy of the /sub 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 0/ transition is currently underway using this narrow probe laser and an octave spanning femtosecond laser. Our most recent results are presented. The proposed measurement technique, accuracy, and stability of an optical clock based on the EIT (electromagnetically-induced-transparency) measurement in /sup 88/Sr are described.

articleTitle: A homemade femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser and super continuum generation with an air-silica microstructure optical fiber
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this work, the authors report the status of the implementation of a femtosecond frequency comb consisting of a homemade femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser whose spectrum is broadened by a microstructure fiber. This frequency comb is going to be initially used in a scheme to directly measure optical frequencies and in an optical clock based on the calcium intercombination transition at 457 THz.

articleTitle: Optical transversal filters
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Recent new methods for photonic signal processing of microwave signals, based on optical delay line structures are described, including novel coherence-free notch filters, and new structures using grating synthesis techniques for multiple wavelength processors.

articleTitle: Studies of the /sup 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 0/ transition in atomic Yb for optical clocks and qubit arrays
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Yb and Sr are both strong candidates for an optical lattice clock as well as for creating useful qubits. Both atoms have experimentally accessible energy level transitions, allowing the atoms to be readily laser-cooled and trapped, and in the case of Yb, Bose-Einstein condensed. While the Sr clock transition has been studied extensively, both in and out of an optical lattice, the same transition in Yb has thus far remained unexplored experimentally. Here we report the direct excitation of the 578 nm /sup 1/S/sub 0/-/sup 3/P/sub 0/ transition in odd isotope /sup 171,173/Yb. We also discuss the possible application of this type of transitions in making qubits for quantum computation and a clock scheme based on three-photon transition in an even isotope.

articleTitle: Remote synchronization of mode-locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Using an intra-cavity electro-optic modulator and PZT we stabilize the repetition frequency of a fiber laser to a high-stability RF reference that is transmitted over a fiber network via optical pulses from a remote laser.

articleTitle: Signal analysis tools applied to the temporal characterization of ultrashort optical pulses
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Concepts for the measurement of the temporal electric field of optical pulses are reviewed. Examples of characterization techniques based on the concepts of spectrography, interferometry and tomography are presented.

articleTitle: Solid-state lasers for frequency metrology
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The unique properties of solid-state laser materials such as ultrawide bandwidth and long upper-state lifetimes enable unique tools for frequency metrology. We report on recent progress in femtosecond laser frequency combs from octave-spanning Ti:sapphire lasers and single-frequency microchip lasers.

articleTitle: Low power, high bit rate CMOS driver for VCSEL used in free space optical interconnect
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We propose a novel driver circuit design using 0.8 micron CMOS technology that drives a 1550 nm VCSEL used in free space optics. We report a distinct improvement in power consumption at 2.5 Gbps.

articleTitle: Fourier synthesis of multicolor femtosecond pulses for attosecond pulse generation
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We have achieved long-term phase locking among multicolor femtosecond pulses by using an optical parametric oscillator and a two-wavelength laser consisting of Ti:sapphire and Cr:forsterite lasers for an attosecond pulse train generation by Fourier synthesis.

articleTitle: Time-frequency analysis of temporal Talbot effect
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: The problem of propagation of a periodic optical pulse sequence through a linear dispersive fiber is investigated in the joint time-frequency domain. This study provides a new and deeper insight into the dynamics of formation of the integer and fractional temporal Talbot patterns which are observed along the fiber propagation distance.

articleTitle: A 600 MHz octave-spanning Ti:sapphire laser for optical frequency measurements and comparisons
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Laser frequency combs based on modelocked femtosecond lasers have enabled a simple means for performing absolute optical frequency measurements and inter-comparisons. In conclusion, using the demonstrated techniques it should be possible to perform measurements and comparisons of optical standards from 300 nm (frequency doubled 600 nm light) to 1200 nm (fundamental light).

articleTitle: Measurement of the quadrupole moment in the mercury ion optical clock
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report a measurement of the /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ 5d/sup 9/6s/sup 2/ /sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ electric quadrupole moment and discuss its implications for the accuracy of an optical clock based upon the /sup 2/D/sub 1/2/(F = 0) /spl harr/ /sup 2/D/sub 5/2/(F = 2) transition at 282 nm.

articleTitle: The RF spectrum of partially polarized light and its application to system characterization
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Formalism for complete characterization of the RF spectrum of partially polarized light is described. The formalism is used to characterize the polarization dependence of the RF spectrum at the output of a PMD/PDL medium.

articleTitle: Phase coherent manipulation of light: from precision spectroscopy to extreme nonlinear optics
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Phase control of wide-bandwidth optical frequency combs enables amazing capabilities in optical frequency measurement and synthesis, optical atomic clocks, united time-frequency spectroscopy, coherent pulse synthesis and manipulation, and deterministic studies in sub-cycle physics.

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb at NIM
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: Absolute measurement of stabilized lasers' optical frequency is an important subject in metrology. The traditional tool for establishing the llnk between Cs atomic frequency standard and an optical frequency is harmonic frequency chain ['I. But, such a harmonic frequency chain is very expensive to built and complicated to operate. Only few national metrology institutes have built these systems. For a country without such facility, such a5 in China, the international comparison of stabilized lasers is the only method to realize this link indirectly. The introduction of optical fkequency comb technique greatly simplifies this work, and a frequency comb system can be used for the routine frequency measurement of many stabilized lasers ranging from visible to infrared r2J [31. Therefore, optical frequency comb system will become an indispensable metrological tool.

articleTitle: Development of a single strontium ion frequency standard at 445 THz at Hz level accuracy and low systematic shift
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We describe our refinement and simplification of a 445-THz (674-nm) reference, which uses a single, cooled strontium ion. A value of 444779044095477 /spl plusmn/ 7 Hz was obtained limited by the current realization of NRC atomic time.

articleTitle: An InP based monolithic FM laser
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: We report the first demonstration of a monolithic optical frequency comb generator using quaternary/quaternary multiple quantum well InP/InGaAsP phase modulator. A line spacing of 26 GHz and a comb width of 2 THz were obtained.

articleTitle: Metaphoric optical computing
publicationTitle: Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the authors use optical wave propagation in nonlinear media as a method for investigating nonlinear dynamical behavior of complex systems that are not optical. The basic idea is to construct an optical system whose nonlinear dynamics are related to the system we wish to simulate. We have shown that there are important classes of computationally difficult problems in finding a suitable optical simulator.
